angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 410,463 km at 72.31 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.8295 +/- 0.0151 mas (same row, RUWE 1.21): 72.31 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.59 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-122 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract): 410,463 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.63 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-122 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4009 +/- 47 K from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-122 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-122 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-122.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.696, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-122 (pscomppars): spectral type M0, from Luo et al. 2018 (http://vizier.u-strasbg.fr/viz-bin/VizieR-3?-source=V/153/stellar4)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-122 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.32 dex, from Castro-González et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-122 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.10237, from Hirano et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract)
